Same issue here on Chinese Windows (code page 936/GBK). The `bash` tool hardcodes `result.stdout.toString("utf8")` at line 173 in `bash.ts`, but Windows system commands output in the system's active code page (GBK on zh-CN). The simple fix would be to detect the system encoding on Windows via `chcp.com` and use the appropriate decoder.

Related issues: #31187, #26882, #31830, #31765

Many Chinese/Japanese/Korean Windows users are affected by this. Please consider fixing it in an upcoming release. Thanks!

Regarding giving DeepSeek the ability to read images, I've got a solution based on OpenCode.

In OpenCode, I successfully built a small plugin that gives DeepSeek and GLM the ability to read images in a roundabout way.

The plugin works by calling a sub-agent that uses a multimodal model within the main conversation that's using the deepseek-v4 model. The sub-agent then produces a structured description of the image content and returns the result to the text model.

The plugin automatically handles things like keeping the context and converting image formats, so you don't lose any conversation history.

All you need to do is upload an image in the DeepSeek chat window, and the plugin takes care of the rest.

To get as close to a native multimodal experience as possible, I divided common image-reading scenarios into different categories. Each category returns a different structured output, which further improves the reading result.

It's still not true native multimodal, but it works really well in AI coding scenarios.

[I wrote a detailed tutorial explaining how to do this](https://www.dataleadsfuture.com/deepseek-v4-cant-read-images-i-made-it-read/), if you're interested.

**Additional data gathered 2026-06-15:**

To test whether startup timing was the key factor, I added a random 0–4 second sleep before each `opencode` invocation, spreading out individual start times. This reduced blank renders within a single group of sessions, but the issue returned once the total number of running Opencode instances crossed approximately 28. Sessions beyond that threshold came up blank regardless of their individual start time offsets.

This suggests the trigger is the total number of concurrent Opencode instances rather than sessions starting at the same instant.

The blank panes are completely empty — no partial frames. The processes are alive and attached to tmux; the TUI simply never paints.

@rekram1-node @simonklee @malventano @marcusquinn I re-checked the local SQLite metadata on OpenCode 1.17.7 and updated this issue plus the sanitized gist.

New finding: this looks like the root cause for the Opus 4.8 failure chain, not just a visible-text leak.

In the affected session, `github-copilot/claude-opus-4.8` sometimes produced assistant messages with:

- `finish = tool-calls`
- zero structured tool parts
- assistant text containing pseudo tool-call markup such as `<invoke ...>` or short `call <tool>` lines

Same-session comparison:

| Model | `<invoke>` text parts | `call ...` text parts | `finish=tool-calls` with 0 tool parts | assistant-prefill API errors |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| `claude-opus-4.6` | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| `claude-opus-4.7` | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| `claude-opus-4.8` | 13 | 229 | 6 | 6 |

So #31807 appears downstream: after one of these malformed `finish=tool-calls` turns, OpenCode continues the loop and the next Copilot Claude request effectively ends with assistant, which triggers the assistant-prefill 400.

Updated sanitized evidence:
https://gist.github.com/doomsday616/d3fb56acd0f14964a9797df35f1fcd96

I also withdrew the earlier workaround PR because the better fix should handle the malformed `finish=tool-calls` / no-tool-part response at the root.

After re-checking local SQLite metadata on OpenCode 1.17.7, the assistant-prefill 400 appears to be downstream of a more specific malformed tool-call response:

- `github-copilot/claude-opus-4.8` sometimes produces assistant text containing pseudo tool-call markup such as `<invoke ...>`.
- The same assistant message is marked `finish=tool-calls`.
- There is no structured tool part.
- The next automatic continuation then effectively sends an assistant-ending request, which Copilot Claude rejects.

This PR was a workaround: it appended a synthetic user turn and scrubbed persisted pseudo tool-call text. That helps symptoms, but the better fix should handle the malformed `finish=tool-calls` / no-tool-part response at the root.

**4. `tui.json` parallel plugin system not documented**

The skill only documents `opencode.json` and never mentions that the TUI has its own `tui.json` config file with a separate `plugin` array — loaded by a completely independent plugin system (`plugin/tui/runtime.ts` vs `plugin/index.ts`). A user removing a plugin from `opencode.json` will find it still active if it's also (or only) declared in `tui.json$/. This is exactly what happened to me today — `@cortexkit/opencode-magic-context` kept loading via `tui.json$ despite being removed from `opencode.jsonc$.
